title: Benz Patent-Motorwagen
summary: On 29 January 1886 Carl Benz of Mannheim applied for a patent on his three-wheeled vehicle with a gas engine, and it was granted on 2 November. Its engine, chassis and drive train were designed from scratch, not added to an existing carriage. He first drove it in public around Mannheim on 3 July 1886. Germany's patent office calls the patent practically the birth certificate of the automobile.

uncertainty.note: Patent applied for on 29 January 1886 and granted on 2 November 1886.

as_recorded.value: ‘Vehicle with gas engine’ (DE37435) is practically the birth certificate of the automobile.

Carl Benz designed it in 1885 and filed for a patent on January 29, 1886. The patent No. 37435, granted by the imperial patent office for this “vehicle with gas-engine drive” was the automobile’s birth certificate.

where.historical_name: Mannheim, Grand Duchy of Baden, German Empire

importance.justification: Considered the first functional automobile with a combustion engine, and the start of motor transport.

sources.title: Bertha Benz: The first driver in history
sources.publisher: German Patent and Trade Mark Office (DPMA)

reviewer_note: The pin is the city of Mannheim, where Benz had his factory; the sources opened do not give its address. One source is the carmaker's own public archive, so its praise was left out.
